verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Both halves are present, the second literally and the first through an encoding. Q_0: fundamentalInterior is {x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) | ∀ i, |x i| < 1/2}, which is exactly the open centred cube (-1/2,1/2)^3 (coordinatewise |x_i| < 1/2 ⇔ -1/2 < x_i < 1/2); the closed cube [-1/2,1/2]^3 is also named, as fundamentalCube, and is used in the support clauses. T^3 = ℝ^3/ℤ^3: the repository never forms the quotient type. Per the module docstring of NavierStokes/ProblemStatement.lean ("The unit torus is represented by periodic functions on Euclidean three-space"), a field on T^3 is a field on Space = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) satisfying UnitSpatialPeriodsOn, i.e. invariance under the three unit coordinate shifts x ↦ x + e_i for all x. The rewriting is the standard identification of functions on ℝ^3/ℤ^3 with ℤ^3-periodic functions on ℝ^3: the lattice ℤ^3 itself is Lattice = (Fin 3 → ℤ), embedded in ℝ^3 by lattice, and invariance under all of it is the content of periodize_add_lattice; quantifying UnitSpatialPeriodsOn over every x and the three generators e_i = lattice (Pi.single i 1) gives invariance under every lattice vector by induction on the three integer coordinates (and so under negative shifts), so the two conditions agree. Noted, not a defect: NavierStokes/PeriodicIntegration.lean:29 uses a second fundamental domain, cube = Icc 0 1 (the corner cube [0,1]^3), for integration over the torus; it is a different fundamental domain for the same ℤ^3, while the clauses that correspond to the paper's Q_0 use the centred cube.
